text:
rachel: Heads-up from support  tenant acme-corp saw a ~4x spike in billed units for a single bulk embeddings call. Customer insists they set X-Embed-Dims=1536.

sam: Oof. do we have the raw request + preflight logs?

rachel: pasted sample (sanitized):
```http
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer ###
Content-Type: application/json
X-Embed-Dims: 1536

{"model":"open-embed-v2","input":["short text 1","short text 2","[LONG BLOB ~6k chars]","short text 3"]}
```

rachel: preflight/logs: 
```
preflight: items=4, sample_lens=[12,13,6020,11]
preflight: header_dims=1536
preflight: inferred_dims_for_items=[1536,1536,8192,1536]
routing: decided=split_batches -> paths=[fastpath,fastpath,slowpath,fastpath]
quota: estimated_units=4*48=192 (based on header)
quota: actual_units=48+48+1024+48=1168
```

tomas: so the header lied (or was overly optimistic). we split the batch because one item needed slowpath. estimate used header dims * item_count, so underbilled estimated_units. That mismatch is rough.

alex: console fallout: tenants see a "bill surprise" in day-0 usage reports and hit alerts. We need a short-term console mitigator: surface "header validation mismatch" in the per-route cost timeline and add an automated note when actual_units > estimated_units * 2.

sam: long-term options: (A) trust header for routing/estimates but validate post-hoc and emit correction/billing adjustment; (B) validate header preflight by sampling content and override estimate when mismatch detected; (C) reject requests with header mismatch with 400 + helpful error. Tradeoffs: A = least user disruption, but causes surprise billing and console noise. B = better estimates but adds preflight CPU and latency; could slow small requests. C = friction for customers but safest billing.

tomas: my preference B but only for large batches or when max_item_len > 2048. For small requests (all items <2k) keep trusting header. Also we can do an async validation path: accept, but immediately recompute estimate and emit an audit event that updates console cost and triggers tenant notification if large delta. That reduces tail latency impact.

billing-bot: Note: We have existing billing smoothing rules but they don't catch this class. Created BILL-762 to review automatic credit rules.

rachel: customer feedback: they used a homegrown SDK that sets X-Embed-Dims=1536 to optimize. They didn't expect it to be validated. They want us to document best practices and maybe offer an SDK helper that computes dims.

alex: UI/telemetry checklist: 1) add boolean badge "dims_header_validated" per request in trace view; 2) metric dim_header_mismatch_rate per tenant; 3) histogram of estimated_units vs billed_units by day; 4) soft-warning banner for tenants with >10 mismatches in 24h.

sam: server plan: implement an "embed header validation" pipeline: sample up to N=5 items or first 10KB, compute inferred_dims_max. If inferred_dims_max > header_dims * 2 then mark mismatch and take action per config: [override-estimate, async-recompute, reject]. Put behind flag `embed_header_validation_mode` with values `none|async|override|reject`. Default async for canary. Canary 2% then 20% then 100% if stable.

tomas: add lightweight metrics: embed.header_check_duration_ms, embed.header_mismatch_count, embed.header_override_count, embed.header_reject_count. Also emit tenant-scoped tag so billing can reconcile.

ops-bot: INF-2902 created: "validate X-Embed-Dims header and mitigate mixed-dim batch billing surprises" assigned to @sam and @rachel.

billing-bot: ACTION: temporary auto-credit rule proposed when actual_units > estimated_units * 3 AND tenant flagged as autopilot=false. Filing BILL-763.

alex: can we also add a console setting to "enforce header validation" per-tenant? some enterprise customers may want strict reject mode to avoid surprises.

sam: yes - add tenant config key `embed_header_validation` with allowed values `none|async|override|reject`. We'll expose in Console under Routes -> Embeddings -> Advanced.

rachel: docs: I'll add a support article "Why you see higher billed units than estimated" that explains header behavior, recommended SDK helpers, and how to opt into reject/override modes.

tomas: small safety: don't run expensive validation for huge single-item uploads >100k chars; just treat as slowpath and tag `no_header_validation_due_to_size`.

sam: schedule: implement async mode first (non-blocking recompute + telemetry + console badge). Canary to 2% Wed. If metrics look good promote. I'll open PR and link infra tests.

rachel: ping me on the PR, I'll coordinate with support to notify affected customers and post a short note in #docs.

alex: thanks team. once telemetry lands I'll mock up a dashboard card for "header mismatch impact" and we'll track top offenders.

rachel: closing loop: customer ok with async approach as long as we notify and update billing if needed. cheers.
